requirements.description: The CLI is invoked as `node dist/index.js stats <path>` and accepts exactly the command `stats` plus exactly one path argument.

On success, the CLI reads the UTF-8 text file at the given path and writes to stdout one JSON object followed by a newline, containing numeric fields `lines`, `words`, and `characters`, with no other stdout output.
`characters` counts Unicode code points in the file content, including whitespace and line-ending characters.
`words` counts maximal runs of non-whitespace characters.

`lines` counts LF-separated records: empty input has zero lines; a final LF terminates the last record without adding an extra line; CRLF also separates lines and both CR and LF count as characters; blank lines count as lines; an empty file succeeds with all zero counts.
Missing files, directory paths, invalid paths, an unrecognized command, and incorrect argument arity each produce a useful message on stderr, nothing on stdout, and a nonzero exit code.
Paths containing spaces are accepted and processed correctly.
The CLI is written in TypeScript and uses only Node.js built-in modules, with no networking, no third-party dependencies, no GUI, and no persistence beyond reading the given file.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Running `node dist/index.js stats <existing-file>` exits with code 0 and stdout contains exactly one line of JSON with keys `lines`, `words`, `characters` and nothing else.
Each value in the emitted JSON object is a number, and the output line is terminated by a newline.
For a file containing multi-byte code points (e.g. an accented character or an emoji), `characters` equals the code point count, not the UTF-16 code unit count or byte count.
For a file containing spaces, tabs, and line endings, those characters are included in `characters`.
For input with multiple consecutive spaces, tabs, or newlines between tokens, each maximal non-whitespace run is counted once as a word and no empty words are produced.
For an empty file, the CLI exits 0 and prints `{"lines":0,"words":0,"characters":0}`.

Content `a
b` reports 2 lines, while `a
b
` also reports 2 lines because the final LF terminates the last record without adding an extra line.
For content `a\r\nb`, the CLI reports 2 lines and 5 characters, showing CRLF separates lines and both CR and LF are counted.
Content consisting only of blank lines (e.g. `\n\n`) reports the corresponding line count (2) rather than 0.
Passing a path that does not exist produces a non-empty stderr message, empty stdout, and a nonzero exit code.
Passing a path that is a directory produces a non-empty stderr message, empty stdout, and a nonzero exit code.
Passing an unrecognized command (e.g. `node dist/index.js foo <path>`) produces a non-empty stderr message, empty stdout, and a nonzero exit code.
Invoking with no path argument, or with more than one path argument, produces a non-empty stderr message, empty stdout, and a nonzero exit code.
A file located at a path containing spaces is processed successfully with exit code 0 and correct counts.
The project builds from TypeScript sources with no third-party runtime dependencies, and a run of the CLI performs no network access or file writes.

constraints: Implemented in TypeScript, compiled so that `node dist/index.js` is the entry point.
Use Node.js built-in modules only; no third-party runtime dependencies.
No networking, no GUI, and no persistence beyond reading the specified file.
Exactly one supported command, `stats`, and exactly one path argument; no additional flags or commands.
On success, stdout must contain only the single JSON object plus a trailing newline; on failure, stdout must be empty.
Failures must exit with a nonzero code and write a useful message to stderr.
ambiguities: Whether a lone CR not followed by LF starts a new line: assumed it does not separate lines but does count as a character.
Behavior on files that are not valid UTF-8: decoding/replacement policy is unspecified.
Whether a BOM at the start of the file is counted as a character: not specified.
Handling of grapheme clusters and combining marks: spec states code points, so clusters are counted as their constituent code points.
Exact nonzero exit code value is unspecified; any nonzero value is acceptable.
Whether JSON output must be compact single-line formatting or may include whitespace, as long as it is one JSON object followed by a newline.
Whether `dist/index.js` is expected to be prebuilt or produced by a documented build step.
outOfScope: Stdin input, multiple file arguments, or recursive/batch file processing.
Encodings other than UTF-8 and explicit BOM handling.
Additional commands, subcommands, flags, or help/version output.
Word counting rules beyond maximal non-whitespace runs (e.g. punctuation handling, locale rules).
Networking, databases, caching, configuration files, or any persistence.
